policy: Preserve distinct source assets even when they share a semantic key. Explicit novelty and sibling-state keys provide negative constraints for base identities, but unsuffixed named characters with multiple ordinary pre-game construction, costume, or print generations remain visual/component pending unless stronger source evidence selects one.

separated_holiday_candidates.catalog_name: Astromech Droid, R2-D2, Red Holiday Sweater

records.reason: The separate R2D2WinterHoliday source key is strong evidence that holiday-themed physical R2-D2 forms should not be used to resolve the ordinary R2D2 asset. The current candidate set exposes only one ordinary legacy R2-D2 implementation, which is insufficient to assume that exact early body/dome generation is the source artwork; preserve the base identity and flag ordinary candidate coverage as incomplete.

systemic_findings: Sibling novelty keys such as R2D2WinterHoliday can safely exclude holiday-form candidates from an unsuffixed base identity.
When a candidate set becomes sparse after excluding explicit novelty forms, mark candidate coverage incomplete instead of treating the remaining old release as uniquely proven.
Multiple source assets sharing one semantic identity must remain independent review/provenance records until visual equivalence is established.
